constraints: Use the same model/version, task fixture, starting source, tool surface and resource ceiling for matched comparisons.

Public GitHub implementation examples must have at least 1,000 stars at evidence check time or be called out as below the eligibility threshold.
invariants: Async scheduling and prompt optimization cannot become correctness, product-acceptance or external-effect authority.
Every detached operation remains bound to exact call/turn/action/effect identity and unresolved effect ambiguity fails closed.
Efficiency claims require matched evidence with fixed model, task semantics, tool surface and resource budget.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Pin Harbor v0.23.0 at commit 1e5c5c6db929a10a140d05e606882c671ae20729 as the neutral outer execution/evaluation substrate. Harbor owns task sandbox lifecycle, trial identity, verifier invocation and raw trial artifacts only; it does not own ExHarness orchestration, product semantics or acceptance.

D2 — Implement one benchmark-only Harbor custom agent class, ExHarnessHarborAgent, for every measured arm. The only arm option is DIRECT_CODEACT or CORE_SYNC; setup, task instruction forwarding, environment, model route, output path and Harbor integration remain identical so the Harbor adapter is not a second varying factor.

D3 — DIRECT_CODEACT and CORE_SYNC share the exact createJavaScriptCodeActStrategy instance configuration, reference JavaScript session executor, model adapter, prompt/task input, shell or fixture capability surface and budgets. DIRECT_CODEACT invokes the strategy through a benchmark-owned minimal runtime shim; CORE_SYNC invokes the same strategy through createAgentRuntime. No product source is modified to make either arm fit the benchmark.

D4 — Keep internal FANOUT and DEPENDENT_CHAIN tasks only as mechanism/calibration probes. External validity uses Terminal-Bench 2.1 dataset terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1 pinned to source commit 7131e4375048a0e408a8fb404b5f499d726b695b with exact task digests recorded in datasetContract.

D5 — Freeze six external development tasks before implementation results: fix-git, cancel-async-tasks, query-optimize, nginx-request-logging, fix-code-vulnerability and sqlite-db-truncate. Reserve git-leak-recovery, pypi-server, kv-store-grpc and sanitize-git-repo as BB-081 held-out tasks; BB-077 live mode must reject held-out execution.

D6 — Before any model comparison, each selected external task must pass Harbor oracle five times in the selected sandbox and nop must fail at least once. Any oracle flake, nop acceptance, task checksum drift or environment mismatch removes the task from the cohort only by starting a new preregistered cohort; it cannot be silently dropped after model results.

D7 — Pin the first live model route to OpenRouter anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 with provider Anthropic and fallback disabled. Preserve provider-reported charged cost as primary billing evidence and independently normalize against the frozen 2026-09-27 table: USD 3/M fresh input, 15/M output, 0.30/M cache read and 3.75/M five-minute cache write.

D8 — Normalize Harbor AgentContext/TrialResult plus ExHarness trace data into HARNESS_RUN_RECORD_V1. Token/cost/cache fields remain nullable; UNKNOWN or PARTIAL usage never becomes zero. Quality is the independent Harbor verifier result and remains orthogonal to termination, provider and infrastructure failure classes.

D9 — Run three paired repeats per development task and arm. Pair by exact task digest + repeat index; alternate arm order DIRECT→CORE, CORE→DIRECT, DIRECT→CORE. Every attempt, retry, timeout and rejected result stays in the ledger. Report paired distributions and medians; uncertainty intervals are descriptive only and no significance claim is made from the small cohort.

D10 — Predeclare the BB-081 candidate gate now, before async results exist: accepted-task rate candidate >= CORE_SYNC; duplicate external effects = 0 and required recovery negatives pass; median normalized provider-cost ratio <= 0.85; median prompt-input-token ratio <= 0.90; median model-turn ratio <= 1.00; median elapsed-time ratio <= 1.10. Missing registered pairs, unknown primary cost/token accounting, task/verifier drift, safety failure or quality regression yields INCONCLUSIVE or KEEP_SYNC, never PROMOTE_ASYNC.

D11 — Measure model work, tool wait and residual harness time from monotonic event intervals instead of estimating token overhead. The benchmark model adapter records each MODEL interval and canonical stable-prefix/dynamic-suffix hashes/bytes; capability wrappers record CALL intervals. Cache reuse is CONFIRMED only from provider cached-token fields, ELIGIBLE when the stable-prefix hash repeats but provider cache data is absent/zero, and UNKNOWN when usage is unavailable. Residual elapsed time is reported as unattributedHarnessMs, not asserted to be polling overhead.
implementationSlices: S1 — Neutral substrate + adapter: add the pinned Harbor custom-agent adapter, upload/install only the declared ExHarness benchmark runtime into each task environment, forward the Harbor instruction verbatim and emit one normalized run record without making a quality judgment.

S2 — Fixed arms: implement DIRECT_CODEACT minimal runtime shim and CORE_SYNC createAgentRuntime arm over the same JavaScript CodeAct strategy/executor/model/capability contracts; deterministic tests prove only the orchestration path differs.

S3 — Dataset boundary: materialize the six internal calibration tasks, the six pinned Terminal-Bench 2.1 development task digests and four held-out digests; implement oracle/nop preflight, fresh reset, pair identity and hard held-out rejection.

S4 — Accounting + measurement: normalize Harbor trial/verifier/timing data and ExHarness model/turn/tool traces into HARNESS_RUN_RECORD_V1; record monotonic MODEL/capability intervals, stable-prefix/dynamic-suffix hashes/bytes, provider-confirmed cache fields, nullable usage/cost and explicit quality/termination/provider/infra dimensions.

S5 — Live baseline: run three alternating-order paired repeats for each registered development task under the frozen OpenRouter/Anthropic route and finite cohort budget; publish raw pair records plus a multidimensional report with no aggregate winner score.

S6 — Gate + Living truth handoff: publish the preregistered BB-081 non-inferiority/efficiency gate and held-out manifest without executing held-out tasks; after verified implementation, update Core-harness Living Docs with the delivered measurement capability, exact limitations and unchanged synchronous support profile.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Harbor v0.23.0 is used only as a neutral sandbox/trial/verifier substrate through one shared ExHarnessHarborAgent adapter, and changing the arm does not change task instruction, environment, model route or Harbor integration.

DIRECT_CODEACT and CORE_SYNC use identical JavaScript CodeAct strategy, executor, model, prompt/task input, capabilities and budgets; the measured varying factor is the direct minimal runtime shim versus createAgentRuntime orchestration.
Internal calibration, external development and BB-081 held-out tasks are separately pinned; external tasks pass preregistered oracle/nop validation and BB-077 cannot execute held-out tasks.
evidenceRequired: Terminal-Bench source commit and task digests
oracle x5 results per selected task
nop negative result per selected task

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every registered attempt yields HARNESS_RUN_RECORD_V1 with exact task/arm/model/environment identities, verifier result, timings, model turns/tool calls and nullable token/cache/cost fields; missing usage is explicit and all attempts remain in denominators.

Independent verifier quality is orthogonal to termination, provider and infrastructure status, so an accepted candidate may coexist with budget/termination failure and a provider failure cannot be silently rewritten as quality rejection.

Per-request and per-capability monotonic intervals plus canonical stable-prefix/dynamic-suffix hashes and byte counts distinguish observed model time, capability wait, overlap, residual harness time and cache eligibility without inventing provider cache or token metrics.
evidenceRequired: stablePrefixSha256/stablePrefixBytes and dynamicSuffixSha256/dynamicSuffixBytes per model request
provider cached/cache-write fields or explicit UNKNOWN
negative case proving repeated prefix hash alone is not a cache hit

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Three paired repeats per development task, alternating arm order, complete attempt accounting and the BB-081 non-inferiority/efficiency gates are frozen before async candidate results are observed.
evidenceRequired: report containing per-pair values and medians

acceptanceCriteria.statement: BB-077 changes benchmark tooling only; it neither changes Core runtime behavior nor promotes an async profile or product acceptance authority.
evidenceRequired: benchmark report contains no product acceptance decision

invariantCoverage.invariant: Async scheduling and prompt optimization cannot become correctness, product-acceptance or external-effect authority.
Every detached operation remains bound to exact call/turn/action/effect identity and unresolved effect ambiguity fails closed.
Efficiency claims require matched evidence with fixed model, task semantics, tool surface and resource budget.

negativeVerificationCases: Changing arm also changes model/provider, prompt, task digest, environment, capability surface or budget and the run is still admitted as matched.
Harbor adapter has arm-specific setup or instruction rewriting that makes the adapter itself a confounder.
A selected Terminal-Bench task has one oracle failure in five or nop is accepted and the cohort silently drops it after model results exist.
BB-077 attempts one of the four held-out Terminal-Bench tasks before BB-081 enables held-out execution.
Provider usage/cost/cache data is missing and the report stores zero or computes a definitive efficiency ratio.
A repeated stable-prefix hash is reported as a confirmed provider cache hit even though cached_tokens/cache_write_tokens are missing or zero.
Elapsed minus model/tool time is labelled polling/heartbeat overhead without an explicit event proving that cause.
A candidate artifact is independently accepted after budget exhaustion but the report changes quality to REJECTED because termination was non-success.
A provider timeout/rate limit produces no candidate and is counted as verifier rejection instead of provider/termination failure with quality NOT_EVALUATED.
Only successful attempts are used in paired medians or a retry replaces the original attempt.
Benchmark changes packages/core-harness/src, Agentic Application source, outer Jev, product acceptance or effect-authority semantics.

Harbor v0.23.0 exposes custom BaseAgent setup/run, isolated environments, AgentContext nullable token/cache/cost fields, TrialResult timing/exception/verifier data and benchmark task/verifier abstractions. Selected as neutral outer substrate, not product runtime.

researchEvidence.eligibility: Benchmark dataset source, not a reusable implementation example; repository is below the >=1,000-star implementation-example threshold.
researchEvidence.finding: Terminal-Bench 2.1 fixes 28 of 89 prior tasks and publishes exact task digests. Used only as pinned external workload data; ExHarness does not infer implementation quality from this repository.
Eligible minimal-agent reference for comparison of loop simplicity, but not used as the isolation control because its prompt/tool loop would add another varying factor.
Eligible modular-agent reference for event/workspace/accounting patterns, not a BB-077 runtime dependency.
Claude Sonnet 4.6 remains listed at USD 3/M input, 15/M output and 0.30/M cached input; profile is frozen for normalization rather than treated as timeless pricing.
OpenRouter documents Sonnet 4.6 cache-read pricing, 1.25x five-minute cache-write pricing and session_id sticky routing; provider cache observations remain non-authoritative.

AgentRuntime synchronously awaits capability execution and model routing exposes generate-call count; JavaScript CodeAct already supplies a bounded strategy/executor seam suitable for a direct-vs-Core orchestration isolation without changing product source.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: One matched baseline runner records accepted outcome, model identity, input/output/cached tokens when available, model turns, tool calls, elapsed time, cost and failure/retry records.
The baseline distinguishes model work from harness wait/poll/heartbeat-like overhead and reports prompt-prefix/cache reuse observations without inventing provider metrics.
A predeclared comparison protocol and non-regression/cost gate are fixed before async implementation results are observed.

sourceAnchors.match: The fixed comparison contract must hold model snapshot, task input, prompt, initial workspace, resource ceilings, artifact extraction and evaluator constant while the harness/profile changes.

arms.DIRECT_CODEACT: Same JavaScript CodeAct strategy/executor/model/capabilities through a benchmark-owned minimal runtime shim; no AgentRuntime orchestration.
arms.CORE_SYNC: Same JavaScript CodeAct strategy/executor/model/capabilities through current createAgentRuntime synchronous orchestration.

benchmarkContract.adapter: One ExHarnessHarborAgent class; arm is a validated option. setup/run paths are otherwise identical. Harbor instruction is forwarded verbatim. Adapter emits /logs/agent/exharness-run.json and populates AgentContext usage without assigning quality.

datasetContract.preflight: For every selected external task, Harbor oracle must pass 5/5 in the selected sandbox and nop must fail >=1/1 before live model dispatch. Any mismatch requires a newly hashed cohort.
datasetContract.reset: Fresh Harbor trial/environment and ExHarness run identity per attempt. No prior model output, task filesystem mutation or ExHarness session state crosses attempts.
datasetContract.leakage: BB-077 live mode permits only internal calibration + external development tasks. Held-out task names/digests may be committed for reservation but instructions/solutions/results are not used for candidate tuning and runner rejects execution until BB-081.

providerContract.session: Unique session_id per attempt; stable within an attempt only.
providerContract.missingUsage: Store null and KNOWN|PARTIAL|UNKNOWN status with reason. Unknown primary cost/token accounting makes efficiency gate INCONCLUSIVE.

failureTaxonomy.rule: Quality comes only from the independent verifier. Termination/provider/infrastructure dimensions never synthesize a quality verdict; if a candidate exists the verifier still runs when safe.

comparisonContract.unit: exact task digest + repeat index + fixed profile hash
comparisonContract.allAttempts: All initial attempts and retries remain in the ledger; retry never overwrites an earlier attempt.
metrics: normalized provider cost per registered attempt
comparisonContract.reporting: Per-run and paired values plus medians/distributions. No opaque aggregate score and no best-of-k filtering.

futurePromotionGate.quality: candidate accepted-task rate >= CORE_SYNC and no declared quality/safety negative regresses
futurePromotionGate.incomplete: missing registered pair, unknown primary cost/token accounting, task/verifier drift, safety failure or quality regression => INCONCLUSIVE or KEEP_SYNC

comparisonContract.uncertainty: Three paired repeats are a bounded engineering experiment, not a significance claim. Bootstrap intervals may be reported descriptively only.

measurementContract.clock: monotonic process clock for benchmark-owned intervals; wall timestamps are metadata only

requestProjection.stablePrefix: canonical serialization of fixed system/protocol instructions, task instruction, capability schema and static context blocks
requestProjection.dynamicSuffix: canonical serialization of turn number, observations, evolving history/prompt context and last validation error

derived.modelCapabilityOverlapMs: intersection duration of MODEL and capability intervals; expected zero for current synchronous arms unless an implementation explicitly overlaps
derived.unattributedHarnessMs: max(0, agentExecutionMs - union(MODEL and capability intervals)); descriptive residual only, never named polling overhead without an explicit event
derived.explicitPollHeartbeatCalls: count only events/capability calls explicitly tagged poll or heartbeat; zero is reportable only when trace completeness is true

cacheStatus.CONFIRMED: provider reports cached_tokens > 0 for the request
cacheStatus.MISS: provider reports cached_tokens = 0 with known usage
cacheStatus.ELIGIBLE: stablePrefixSha256 repeats within the attempt but provider cache usage is unavailable; not a claimed hit
cacheStatus.UNKNOWN: stable prefix or provider usage needed for classification is unavailable

measurementContract.rule: Never infer provider token counts, cache hits or causal overhead from byte counts or elapsed subtraction. Byte/hash projections establish prompt stability only.

livingDocs.statement: BB-077 Living Docs describe only the delivered benchmark/harness-measurement capability, fixed-factor contract, accounting limitations and current synchronous baseline; they do not claim async promotion or product-value results that BB-081/BB-074 have not established.
